strings.SVI_progressivism_1_party_long: People's Political Party - Federated Industrial Allied Workers Union
strings.SVI_Banana_Boom_desc:
The Windward Islands' sugar industry was dying, the gutshot of Caribbean competition and the rise of sugar beets were slowly draining the islands dry. Only through the large-scale foreign investment in the production of bananas was the bleeding plugged.

The islands have since been profoundly transformed by the so-called 'Banana Boom', with capital and infrastructure development flowing in—but the banana firms, most notably the infamous United Fruit Company, have not been idle, and now throw around significant weight in political and social matters.
strings.SVI_Neocolonial_Backlash_desc: The plantation farming of old's revival in the form of the banana harvest has brought great wealth, but skyrocketed social tensions. Worker protections in the islands have never been substantial, and this, combined with negligible political representation—even by the Caribbean's standards—has brought things to a low boil. A backlash against this new, 'prosperous' order stirs beneath the glittering surface.
strings.SVI_Sifting_Through_The_Ashes_desc:
In 1902, the volcano La Soufrière erupted, killing some 1,600 people, making another 4,000 homeless, and destroying St. Vincent's cotton industry. In [year when this event happens], the West Indies Federation collapsed before it could even be created, and under the rubble lay St. Vincent and its arrowroot and banana economy. To the rest of its Windward island brethren, St. Vincent lies as a warning of what an underdeveloped and undiverse economy may do to them.

Now the island is almost entirely reliant on foreign aid, mostly from the West Indies Commission, to stay out of bankruptcy. Everyday, representatives from St. Vincent request aid from other nations, and each time the nations respond, “We'll see,” and St. Vincent must hope that they feel generous, lest the island sink.
strings.SVI_Shadow_of_La_Soufriere: In the Shadow of La Soufrière
strings.SVI_Shadow_of_La_Soufriere_desc:
When one talks about St. Vincent and the Grenadines, the Grenadines are scarcely mentioned, if at all. Nearly the entire economy and political structure of the nation relies on St. Vincent, with its other islands being underdeveloped and distant from the central government. Some islands have even remained untouched since the 19th century.

The few inhabitants of these islands rarely call themselves Vincentian, and they've also begun to form their own separatist groups. While the Grenadines may lay dormant for now, they'll overflow soon and engulf St. Vincent like La Soufrière in 1902.
